claims.text: Representative large vision-language models suffer from severe object hallucination issues.
Objects that frequently appear in visual instructions are prone to be hallucinated by large vision-language models.
Objects that co-occur with image objects are prone to be hallucinated by large vision-language models.
POPE evaluates object hallucination via a polling-based query method.

evidence.description: Evaluation experiments conducted on several representative LVLMs showed widespread object hallucination.
Analysis of visual instructions indicated a correlation between high object frequency in instructions and hallucination rate.
Analysis showed objects co-occurring with target image objects were significantly more prone to hallucination.

methodologies.name: POPE (Polling-based Object Probe Evaluation)
methodologies.description: A polling-based query method designed to evaluate object hallucination in large vision-language models.

limitations.text: Large vision-language models tend to generate objects inconsistent with target images in descriptions.
